key_insight: Randomized block coordinate descent can generalize well for nonconvex learning, with provable high-probability bounds on population-risk gradients and suboptimality under standard smoothness assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The results justify using RBCD with early stopping and tuned step sizes as a practical large-scale optimizer for high-dimensional nonconvex machine learning models.
method: Derive high-probability generalization bounds for empirical and population gradients in the nonconvex setting.
Use polynomially decaying step sizes and select the iteration count to balance optimization error and generalization error.
Extend the analysis to gradient-dominated objectives and a structured-loss setting to obtain dimension-independent guarantees.
evidence_signal: The paper is a theory-only analysis that derives probabilistic bounds from the abstract, rather than reporting empirical benchmark results.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on smoothness and carefully tuned step-size/early-stopping schedules, so practical performance may degrade if these assumptions are violated.
paper_title: Generalization Guarantees of Randomized Block Coordinate Descent for Nonconvex Learning
